When type is RAUC_DM_VERITY, root_digest and salt must be provided; when RAUC_DM_CRYPT, key is used. Enumeration of error codes for the eMMC helper API. Values indicate general failure, ioctl-related failure, a user data area (UDA) boot partition condition, or an invalid boot partition selection. Intended for use with GLib error handling (see R_EMMC_ERROR quark).

Enumeration of runtime states for a slot. Values support bitwise flags: ST_ACTIVE (1), ST_INACTIVE (2), and ST_BOOTED (5, i.e., 4 | ST_ACTIVE) with ST_UNKNOWN as default. Used in RaucSlot.state and conversion helpers.
Holds persisted and runtime metadata about a slot’s installed bundle and activation history, including checksums, build info, status string, install/activation timestamps and counters.

Describes a system slot, including identification, class, device and filesystem properties, bootloader name, flags controlling update behavior, region sizing, runtime state, relationships (parent/children via parent pointer), mount points, and an associated RaucSlotStatus.

Opaque-forward-declared, then fully defined struct representing a configured event logger for RAUC structured logs. Holds configuration (name, target file, event filters, output format, rotation limits) and runtime state (configured/broken flags, current size, output stream) plus a writer callback that emits a single structured log record.
Enumeration selecting the on-disk/output format for event logging: full readable, short readable, compact JSON, or pretty-printed JSON.

Enumeration of error codes for the NBD component, covering configuration, startup, I/O, HTTP-related conditions mapped to errors, and shutdown. Used with the GLib error domain returned by r_nbd_error_quark(). Note: this is an enum type; pointer usage is uncommon except for API uniformity.

Opaque-ish configuration-and-state container for a kernel NBD device handled by this API. Holds socket FD, device index/validity, device name string, and data size. Created and freed via r_nbd_new_device()/r_nbd_free_device().

Configuration and runtime state for an NBD server helper. Contains connection/socket, spawned subprocess handle, TLS credentials/flags, request headers, and information discovered from the remote (size, effective URL, timestamps, ETag). Construct with r_nbd_new_server() and release with r_nbd_free_server().
Error domain-specific enumeration for hash-index operations. Values indicate common failure reasons: size mismatch, not found, or data modified. Used with GError tagged by r_hash_index_error_quark().
Fixed-size container representing a single indexed chunk and its hash. Holds 4096 bytes of chunk data and the corresponding 32-byte hash. Intended to be filled by r_hash_index_get_chunk().

	gchar *label; /* label for debugging */
	int data_fd; /* file descriptor of the indexed data */
	guint32 count; /* number of chunks */

objects.description: Opaque-ish struct describing an index of fixed-size chunks for a data file, along with their hashes and lookup structures. Instances are created via r_hash_index_open/reuse/open_slot/open_image and must be freed with r_hash_index_free.

Struct holding flags for install-time hooks defined at manifest level. Currently only tracks whether an install_check hook is present/enabled.

Manifest image entry describing one artifact image: slot class, artifact and variant identifiers, checksum, source filename, image type (possibly auto-detected), per-image hooks, conversion/adapter instructions, and list of converted output filenames.
Enumeration of bundle/manifest formats: plain, verity (dm-verity metadata), and crypt (encrypted). Note: this is an enum; pointer type shown per requirements.

Top-level manifest data structure describing an update bundle: compatibility/version metadata, bundle format and related parameters (verity/crypt), handler and hook configuration, list of images, arbitrary metadata map, flags, computed hash, and collected warnings.

Represents a single artifact stored in a repository, including bundle metadata, a checksum of its contents, references (parent relations), and repo-managed paths for installation/state. The repo pointer links back to its containing RArtifactRepo.

Container and manager for artifacts. Tracks metadata (name, description, path, type, parent_class), per-repo data directory, stored artifacts map, possible parent references, and runtime-type-specific data (currently a composefs section with a local object store).

objects.definition:
typedef enum {
	CHECK_BUNDLE_DEFAULT       = 0,
	/* skip BIT(0) for now to avoid interpreting a TRUE as NO_VERIFY by mistake */
	CHECK_BUNDLE_NO_VERIFY     = BIT(1),      // If not set the bundle signature
	                                          // will be verified, if set this
	                                          // step will be skipped.
	CHECK_BUNDLE_NO_CHECK_TIME = BIT(2),      // If set, X509_V_FLAG_NO_CHECK_TIME
	                                          // is passed to openssl to suppress
	                                          // checking the validity period of
	                                          // certificates and CRLs against
	                                          // the current time.
	CHECK_BUNDLE_TRUST_ENV     = BIT(3),      // If set, the runtime environment
	                                          // is fully trusted and no attempts
	                                          // will be made to protect against
	                                          // concurrent modification of the
	                                          // bundle.
} CheckBundleParams;
objects.description: Bit-field flags controlling bundle checking behavior: skip signature verification, skip certificate time checks, and trust the runtime environment. Used as the params argument to functions operating on bundles.

Holds runtime information related to an installation, currently only the bundle that is mounted by RAUC during an installation operation.
Enumeration of configuration modes for the global RAUC context: no config, auto-load if present, or required.
Represents a single override entry for a configuration file: section, key name, and value to apply over the loaded config.

Global RAUC context holding configuration, status, progress tracking, signing settings, system information, optional handler args, and per-installation runtime info. It also maintains busy/pending state and test-only mock data.
Represents a progress tracking step with optional weighting, substep counters, and percentage bookkeeping. Used as nodes in the progress stack maintained by RaucContext.

functions.name: r_utils_error_quark
functions.description: Returns the GQuark identifying the RUtils error domain (used with GError). Typical usage is via the R_UTILS_ERROR macro to check/set GError domains.
requirements: No arguments.
Intended for use with GError APIs; compare/error->domain against the returned quark.

functions.name: close_preserve_errno
functions.description: Closes a POSIX file descriptor while preserving errno across the close call. Useful in cleanup paths where you must not clobber a previously set errno.
requirements: fd may be -1 to indicate 'no fd' (per the associated g_auto cleanup pattern).
fd must be a valid open file descriptor or -1.
Caller should not use fd after this call.

functions.name: r_subprocess_new
functions.description: Creates a new GSubprocess with the given flags from argv-style arguments. argv0 is the program path/name followed by arguments, terminated implicitly by the varargs end. Returns the started subprocess object on success.
requirements: argv0 must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string.
Varargs must supply subsequent arguments and be terminated by a NULL sentinel (standard GLib argv varargs pattern).
If error is non-NULL, *error must be NULL on entry (GLib convention).
flags must be a valid combination of GSubprocessFlags.

functions.name: r_subprocess_runv
functions.description: Starts a subprocess defined by a NULL-terminated array of argument strings and waits for it to finish. Convenience wrapper around GLib subprocess APIs.
requirements: args must be non-NULL and contain a NULL terminator as the last element (args->pdata[args->len-1] == NULL).
args must contain at least one program path/name element.
Each element (except the final NULL terminator) must be a valid NUL-terminated string.
If error is non-NULL, *error must be NULL on entry (GLib convention).
flags must be a valid combination of GSubprocessFlags.

functions.name: r_ptr_array_add_printf
functions.description: Formats a string with printf-style formatting and appends a newly allocated copy to the end of a GPtrArray. Shorter alternative to using g_strdup_printf and g_ptr_array_add separately.
requirements: ptrarray must be a valid, initialized GPtrArray*.
format must be a non-NULL printf-style format string.
Varargs must match the format string.

functions.name: r_ptr_array_env_to_shell
functions.description: Converts an array of 'key=value' strings to a single shell-quoted string suitable for shell-parsable output.
requirements: ptrarray must be a valid GPtrArray* (may be empty).
Each element of ptrarray should be a NUL-terminated string of the form key=value (as per documentation).
Returns a newly allocated string which the caller must free with g_free().

functions.name: r_environ_setenv_ptr_array
functions.description: Calls g_environ_setenv for each 'key=value' string in ptrarray, adding/updating entries in the provided environment list.
requirements: envp may be NULL (as accepted by g_environ_setenv) or a NULL-terminated environment array.
ptrarray must be a valid GPtrArray*; each element should be 'key=value'.
overwrite determines whether existing variables are changed (passed through to g_environ_setenv).
Returns a newly allocated environment array which the caller must free with g_strfreev().

functions.name: r_subprocess_launcher_setenv_ptr_array
functions.description: Sets environment variables on a GSubprocessLauncher for each 'key=value' string in ptrarray, via g_subprocess_launcher_setenv.
requirements: launcher must be a valid, initialized GSubprocessLauncher*.
ptrarray must be a valid GPtrArray*; each element should be 'key=value'.
overwrite controls whether existing variables on the launcher are replaced.

functions.name: read_file
functions.description: Reads a file’s contents into a new GBytes object.
requirements: filename must be a non-NULL path to a readable regular file.
If error is non-NULL, *error must be NULL on entry (GLib convention).
On success, caller owns the returned GBytes and must unref with g_bytes_unref().

functions.name: read_file_str
functions.description: Reads a file’s contents into a newly allocated NUL-terminated string.
requirements: filename must be a non-NULL path to a readable file.
If error is non-NULL, *error must be NULL on entry (GLib convention).
Caller must free the returned string with g_free().

functions.name: write_file
functions.description: Writes the content of a GBytes to the specified file path.
requirements: filename must be a non-NULL path; the process must have permission to create/overwrite the target as needed.
bytes must be a non-NULL GBytes* containing data to write.
If error is non-NULL, *error must be NULL on entry (GLib convention).

functions.name: copy_file
functions.signature: gboolean copy_file(const gchar *srcprefix, const gchar *srcfile, const gchar *dstprefix, const gchar *dstfile, GError **error);
functions.description: Copies a file from source to destination. Supports optional prefix paths concatenated with file names.
requirements: srcfile and dstfile must be non-NULL NUL-terminated strings.
srcprefix and dstprefix, if provided, must be valid path prefixes or NULL (exact handling of NULL prefixes is not documented; behavior of prefix concatenation is inferred).
The source file must exist and be readable; destination path must be creatable/writable.
If error is non-NULL, *error must be NULL on entry (GLib convention).

functions.name: rm_tree
functions.description: Recursively deletes the contents of a directory (and likely the directory itself, by inference).
requirements: path must be a non-NULL path to a directory tree that the process is allowed to modify.
If error is non-NULL, *error must be NULL on entry (GLib convention).

functions.name: r_tree_check_open
functions.description: Recursively checks a directory tree for open files and reports whether any are open.
requirements: path must be a non-NULL directory path.
If error is non-NULL, *error must be NULL on entry (GLib convention).
Returns TRUE if no files are open; FALSE otherwise (per documentation).

functions.name: resolve_path
functions.description: Resolves path to an absolute path using basefile’s directory or the current working directory. If path is already absolute, it is returned as-is. Otherwise, if basefile is absolute, uses its directory as the prefix; if basefile is relative or NULL, uses the current working directory.
requirements: path must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string.
basefile may be NULL or a NUL-terminated string; if non-NULL and absolute, its directory will be used as base.
Returns a newly allocated absolute path on success that the caller must free with g_free().

functions.name: resolve_path_take
functions.description: Like resolve_path(), but consumes and frees the input path argument. Intended for cases where the original path string is not needed after resolution.
requirements: path must be a dynamically allocated, mutable string suitable for freeing (e.g., via g_free). Caller must not use path after the call.
basefile may be NULL or a NUL-terminated string.
Returns a newly allocated absolute path on success; caller must free it with g_free().

functions.name: check_remaining_groups
functions.description: Validates that there are no unexpected or remaining groups in a GKeyFile after expected parsing is done. Exact criteria are inferred from the name.
requirements: key_file must be a valid, initialized GKeyFile* already loaded with data.
If error is non-NULL, *error must be NULL on entry (GLib convention).

functions.name: check_remaining_keys
functions.description: Validates that there are no unexpected or remaining keys in a specified group of a GKeyFile after expected parsing. Exact criteria are inferred from the name.
requirements: key_file must be a valid, initialized GKeyFile*.
groupname must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string naming an existing group.
If error is non-NULL, *error must be NULL on entry (GLib convention).

functions.name: key_file_consume_string
functions.signature: gchar * key_file_consume_string(GKeyFile *key_file, const gchar *group_name, const gchar *key, GError **error);
functions.description: Retrieves a string value for key from group_name in key_file and removes the key from the file. Returns a newly allocated string or NULL on error.
requirements: key_file must be a valid GKeyFile*.
group_name and key must be non-NULL NUL-terminated strings and must exist in key_file.
If error is non-NULL, *error must be NULL on entry (GLib convention).
Caller must free the returned string with g_free().

functions.name: value_check_tab_whitespace
functions.description: Checks that the input string contains neither whitespace nor tab characters. Returns TRUE if the string is free of whitespace/tab; FALSE otherwise.
requirements: str must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated string to validate.
If error is non-NULL, *error must be NULL on entry (GLib convention).

functions.name: key_file_consume_integer
functions.signature: gint key_file_consume_integer(GKeyFile *key_file, const gchar *group_name, const gchar *key, GError **error);
functions.description: Retrieves an integer value for key from group_name in key_file, removes the key, and returns the integer value.
requirements: key_file must be a valid GKeyFile*.
group_name and key must be non-NULL NUL-terminated strings and must exist in key_file with an integer value.
If error is non-NULL, *error must be NULL on entry (GLib convention).

functions.name: key_file_consume_binary_suffixed_string
functions.signature: guint64 key_file_consume_binary_suffixed_string(GKeyFile *key_file, const gchar *group_name, const gchar *key, GError **error);
functions.description: Parses a binary-suffixed numeric string (e.g., with KiB/MiB) from key in group_name, removes the key, and returns the value as bytes (inferred from name).
requirements: key_file must be a valid GKeyFile*.
group_name and key must be non-NULL NUL-terminated strings and must exist in key_file with a parseable binary-suffixed numeric value.
If error is non-NULL, *error must be NULL on entry (GLib convention).

functions.name: r_realpath
functions.description: Returns the canonicalized absolute pathname corresponding to path (realpath-like).
requirements: path must be a non-NULL NUL-terminated path string that should exist in the filesystem.
Returns a newly allocated string; caller must free it with g_free().

functions.name: r_whitespace_removed
functions.description: Removes surrounding whitespace from the string in place and returns TRUE if any whitespace was removed, FALSE otherwise.
requirements: str must point to a mutable, NUL-terminated character buffer.
Caller must ensure the buffer is writable.

functions.name: r_hex_decode
functions.description: Decodes a hex-encoded string buffer of length len into raw bytes. Returns a newly allocated byte buffer.
requirements: hex must be a non-NULL buffer of length len containing only hexadecimal characters 0-9, a-f, A-F.
len should be even (required for pairs of hex digits).
Returns a newly allocated buffer; caller must free with g_free() (inferred GLib allocator usage).

functions.name: r_hex_encode
functions.description: Encodes a raw byte buffer of length len into a hex string. Returns a newly allocated NUL-terminated string.
requirements: raw must be a non-NULL pointer to at least len bytes of data.
len may be zero to encode an empty buffer.
Caller must free the returned string with g_free().

functions.name: r_read_exact
functions.signature: gboolean r_read_exact(const int fd, guint8 *data, size_t size, GError **error);
functions.description: Reads exactly size bytes from fd into data, retrying as needed. Returns FALSE on error or short read and may set error.
requirements: fd must be a valid open file descriptor readable by the process.
data must point to a buffer of at least size bytes.
If error is non-NULL, *error must be NULL on entry (GLib convention).

functions.name: r_write_exact
functions.signature: gboolean r_write_exact(const int fd, const guint8 *data, size_t size, GError **error);
functions.description: Writes exactly size bytes from data to fd, retrying as needed. Returns FALSE on error or short write and may set error.
requirements: fd must be a valid open file descriptor writable by the process.
data must point to a buffer of at least size bytes.
If error is non-NULL, *error must be NULL on entry (GLib convention).

functions.name: r_pread_exact
functions.signature: gboolean r_pread_exact(const int fd, guint8 *data, size_t size, off_t offset, GError **error);
functions.description: Reads exactly size bytes from fd at the given offset into data using pread semantics (does not change file position).
requirements: fd must be a valid open file descriptor supporting pread (seekable).
data must point to a buffer of at least size bytes.
offset must be >= 0 (inferred from POSIX pread).
If error is non-NULL, *error must be NULL on entry (GLib convention).

functions.name: r_pwrite_exact
functions.signature: gboolean r_pwrite_exact(const int fd, const guint8 *data, size_t size, off_t offset, GError **error);
functions.description: Writes exactly size bytes to fd at the given offset using pwrite semantics (does not change file position).
requirements: fd must be a valid open file descriptor supporting pwrite (seekable and writable).
data must point to at least size bytes.
offset must be >= 0 (inferred from POSIX pwrite).

functions.name: r_event_log_setup_logger

functions.name: r_event_log_free_logger
functions.description: Frees an REventLogger structure and its associated resources.

After this call, the logger pointer becomes invalid and must not be used.

functions.name: r_event_log_message
functions.description: Convenience function to emit an event log entry for a given event type, formatting the message with printf-style varargs. Intended for modules to easily log structured RAUC events.

functions.name: r_nbd_error_quark
functions.description: Returns the GLib error domain quark for R_NBD_ERROR, to be used with GError when reporting NBD-related errors. Typical usage: pass R_NBD_ERROR as the error domain (via this quark) when setting or checking GErrors produced by these APIs.

Use the returned GQuark as the error domain when creating or matching GError instances for this library.

functions.name: r_nbd_new_device
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new RaucNBDDevice structure for configuring a kernel NBD device. Use r_nbd_free_device to free. The returned struct holds configuration and state (e.g., sock, index, dev, data_size).

Returned pointer may be NULL only on allocation failure (not specified, but typical); callers should check for NULL before use.

functions.name: r_nbd_free_device

functions.name: r_nbd_new_server
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new RaucNBDServer structure used to configure and control an NBD server process/connection (URL, TLS options, headers). Free with r_nbd_free_server.

functions.name: r_nbd_free_server
functions.description: Frees a RaucNBDServer previously created by r_nbd_new_server and releases associated resources, including any GSubprocess and allocated strings/arrays within the struct.
requirements: nbd_srv must either be a valid pointer obtained from r_nbd_new_server or NULL.
Calling with NULL is a no-op (common GLib convention; exact behavior not explicitly stated).

functions.name: r_nbd_setup_device
functions.description: Configures a Network Block Device (NBD) in the kernel using parameters from nbd_dev and returns the resulting device file descriptor via devicefd and the device name inside nbd_dev. Returns TRUE on success, FALSE on failure with error set.
requirements: nbd_dev must be a non-NULL, initialized RaucNBDDevice instance.
devicefd must be a non-NULL pointer to int to receive the opened NBD device file descriptor.
On failure, function returns FALSE and may set *error with domain R_NBD_ERROR; caller must pass a valid GError** (or NULL to ignore errors) and clear/free any set errors.
On success, the device name is stored in nbd_dev->dev; callers should not free or modify internal fields except via provided APIs.
Caller is responsible for eventually removing the device via r_nbd_remove_device and closing any returned file descriptor.

functions.name: r_nbd_remove_device
functions.description: Removes a previously configured kernel NBD device described by nbd_dev. Returns TRUE on success; on failure returns FALSE and sets error.
requirements: nbd_dev must be non-NULL and refer to a device previously set up (e.g., via r_nbd_setup_device).
On failure, returns FALSE and may set *error with domain R_NBD_ERROR; caller must pass a valid GError** (or NULL to ignore) and free any set error.
Any open file descriptors associated with the device should be handled/closed by the caller as appropriate (inferred from typical patterns).

functions.name: r_nbd_run_server
functions.description: Runs the NBD server logic bound to an already-open socket file descriptor sock (likely used in the server subprocess). Returns TRUE on success, FALSE on error.
requirements: sock must be a valid, open socket file descriptor suitable for NBD protocol communication.
On failure, returns FALSE and may set *error with domain R_NBD_ERROR; caller must pass a valid GError** (or NULL to ignore) and free any set error.
This function is intended to be called in a server context; behavior in other contexts is unspecified (inferred).

functions.name: r_nbd_start_server
functions.description: Starts the NBD server according to the configuration in nbd_srv (e.g., URL, TLS options, headers). Likely launches a subprocess and prepares communication. Returns TRUE on success; FALSE with error set on failure. Details beyond the visible struct fields are not documented in this header.
requirements: nbd_srv must be a non-NULL, initialized RaucNBDServer instance.
Configuration fields in nbd_srv should be set appropriately before calling (e.g., url, TLS parameters, headers) — inferred from struct; exact mandatory fields are not specified.

Should be paired with r_nbd_stop_server to cleanly shut down (inferred).

functions.name: r_nbd_stop_server
functions.description: Stops a server previously started with r_nbd_start_server and cleans up associated resources (e.g., subprocess, socket). Returns TRUE on success; FALSE with error set on failure.
requirements: nbd_srv must be non-NULL and refer to a server previously started with r_nbd_start_server (inferred).
On failure, returns FALSE and may set *error with domain R_NBD_ERROR; caller must pass a valid GError** (or NULL to ignore) and free any set error.

functions.name: r_nbd_read
functions.signature: gboolean r_nbd_read(gint sock, guint8 *data, size_t size, off_t offset, GError **error);
functions.description: Reads size bytes from the remote block device via the NBD connection on socket sock starting at byte offset offset into the buffer data. Returns TRUE on success; FALSE on error with error set.
requirements: sock must be a valid, open socket connected to the NBD server handling read requests.
data must be a non-NULL pointer to a buffer of at least size bytes.
size may be zero or greater; typical usage is size > 0. Exact limits are not specified.
offset should be a non-negative byte offset within the remote device; bounds are not specified in the header.
On failure, returns FALSE and may set *error with domain R_NBD_ERROR; caller must pass a valid GError** (or NULL to ignore) and free any set error.

functions.name: network_init
functions.description: Initializes the networking subsystem for this library, setting up libcurl. When ENABLE_NETWORK is not defined, this function is a no-op that always returns TRUE. Typical usage is to call this once before any functions that perform network operations.
requirements: Caller must check the gboolean return value (function is annotated G_GNUC_WARN_UNUSED_RESULT).
If error is non-NULL, it must point to a NULL GError* on entry, and on failure it may be set by the function (GLib GError convention).
Should be called before invoking other network-related functions in this library (inferred from "Network initialization routine" and "Sets up libcurl").
Thread-safety and re-entrancy are unknown; do not assume it is safe to call concurrently or multiple times without documentation.

functions.name: download_file
functions.signature: gboolean download_file(const gchar *target, const gchar *url, goffset limit, GError **error)
functions.description: Downloads data from the given URL to the target path, optionally enforcing a byte limit. Returns TRUE on success and FALSE on failure with details in GError. functions.name: r_hash_index_error_quark
functions.description: Returns the GQuark identifying the Rauc hash index error domain. Use this to check GError domains returned by hash index APIs.
requirements: No arguments; safe to call at any time.
Use the returned GQuark to compare against GError->domain for errors produced by this API.

functions.name: r_hash_index_open
functions.signature: RaucHashIndex *r_hash_index_open(const gchar *label, int data_fd, const gchar *hashes_filename, GError **error);
functions.description: Creates and returns a hash index for an open file descriptor, or reuses an existing raw index file if hashes_filename is provided. On error, returns NULL and sets a GError in the R_HASH_INDEX_ERROR domain.
requirements: label should be a valid, NUL-terminated string used for identification/debugging (non-NULL recommended).
data_fd must be a valid open file descriptor for the data to be indexed, open with appropriate permissions for reading.
hashes_filename may be NULL; if non-NULL, it must reference an existing readable raw hash index file compatible with this API.
If error is non-NULL, it must point to a NULL GError* on entry; on failure it will be set.
The caller must check the return value (warn-unused-result) and free the returned RaucHashIndex with r_hash_index_free().

functions.name: r_hash_index_reuse
functions.signature: RaucHashIndex *r_hash_index_reuse(const gchar *label, const RaucHashIndex *idx, int new_data_fd, GError **error);
functions.description: Reuses an existing hash index with a new file descriptor, enabling lookups against newly written data without rebuilding a separate index. Returns a newly allocated RaucHashIndex sharing the index data but bound to new_data_fd.
requirements: label should be a valid, NUL-terminated string used for identification/debugging (non-NULL recommended).
idx must be a valid RaucHashIndex previously returned by r_hash_index_open/open_slot/open_image and not yet freed.
new_data_fd must be a valid open file descriptor associated with the data to be searched, readable as needed.
If error is non-NULL, it must point to a NULL GError* on entry; on failure it will be set.
The caller must check the return value (warn-unused-result) and free the returned RaucHashIndex with r_hash_index_free().

functions.name: r_hash_index_open_slot
functions.signature: RaucHashIndex *r_hash_index_open_slot(const gchar *label, const RaucSlot *slot, int flags, GError **error);
functions.description: Creates a hash index for the given slot. Attempts to load a previously stored block-hash-index from the slot’s latest hash directory; if not available, builds a new index from the slot device using g_open() with the provided flags.
requirements: label should be a valid, NUL-terminated string used for identification/debugging (non-NULL recommended).
slot must point to a valid RaucSlot object representing the target slot.
flags are passed to g_open(); they must be appropriate for opening the slot device for reading (and any other required mode).
If error is non-NULL, it must point to a NULL GError* on entry; on failure it will be set.
The caller must check the return value (warn-unused-result) and free the returned RaucHashIndex with r_hash_index_free().

functions.name: r_hash_index_open_image
functions.description: Creates a hash index for the given image by loading a previously stored <image>.block-hash-index from the bundle; builds or uses index data associated with the image for lookups and matching.
requirements: label should be a valid, NUL-terminated string used for identification/debugging (non-NULL recommended).
image must point to a valid RaucImage object referring to the desired image/bundle.
If error is non-NULL, it must point to a NULL GError* on entry; on failure it will be set.
The caller must check the return value (warn-unused-result) and free the returned RaucHashIndex with r_hash_index_free().

functions.name: r_hash_index_export
functions.signature: gboolean r_hash_index_export(const RaucHashIndex *idx, const gchar *hashes_filename, GError **error);
functions.description: Exports the raw hash index to the specified file. Returns TRUE on success, FALSE on failure with a GError set.
requirements: idx must be a valid, initialized RaucHashIndex created by this API and not yet freed.
hashes_filename must be a valid, NUL-terminated path where the caller has permission to create/overwrite the file.
If error is non-NULL, it must point to a NULL GError* on entry; on failure it will be set.
The caller must check the boolean return value (warn-unused-result) and handle FALSE by consulting error.

functions.name: r_hash_index_export_slot
functions.signature: gboolean r_hash_index_export_slot(const RaucHashIndex *idx, const RaucSlot *slot, const RaucChecksum *checksum, GError **error);
functions.description: Writes the raw hash index to the slot’s data directory using a filename derived from the provided image checksum. Returns TRUE on success, FALSE on failure with a GError set.
requirements: idx must be a valid, initialized RaucHashIndex created by this API and not yet freed.
slot must point to a valid RaucSlot with an accessible data directory.
checksum must point to a valid RaucChecksum representing the image checksum used to derive the target filename.
If error is non-NULL, it must point to a NULL GError* on entry; on failure it will be set.
The caller must check the boolean return value (warn-unused-result) and handle FALSE by consulting error.

functions.name: r_hash_index_get_chunk
functions.signature: gboolean r_hash_index_get_chunk(const RaucHashIndex *idx, const guint8 *hash, RaucHashIndexChunk *chunk, GError **error);
functions.description: Searches the hash index for the given hash. On success, returns TRUE and fills chunk with reliable data corresponding to the found entry. On failure or not found, returns FALSE and sets a GError indicating the reason (e.g., not found, size/modified).
requirements: idx must be a valid, initialized RaucHashIndex created by this API and not yet freed.
hash must point to a 32-byte digest buffer (the index uses 32-byte hashes).
chunk must be a non-NULL pointer to writable storage; on success its data (4096 bytes) and hash (32 bytes) fields will be populated.
If error is non-NULL, it must point to a NULL GError* on entry; on failure it will be set, typically with domain r_hash_index_error_quark() and a code from RHashIndexErrorError.
The caller must check the boolean return value (warn-unused-result); on FALSE do not use data in chunk as reliable.

functions.name: r_hash_index_free
functions.description: Frees a RaucHashIndex and associated resources. Safe to call with NULL.
requirements: idx may be NULL; if non-NULL it must be a RaucHashIndex obtained from this API and not already freed.
After calling, idx must not be used again.

functions.name: r_signature_free_x509_stack
functions.description: Frees an OpenSSL STACK_OF(X509) container (structure only) without freeing its X509 elements. Intended as a GLib autoptr cleanup for stacks where element ownership is retained elsewhere.
requirements: stack is a pointer to a STACK_OF(X509) previously allocated/obtained by the caller.

Behavior for stack == NULL is unknown (likely a no-op by convention); avoid passing invalid pointers.

functions.name: r_signature_free_x509_stack_pop
functions.description: Frees an OpenSSL STACK_OF(X509) including all contained X509 elements. Intended as a GLib autoptr cleanup when transferring full ownership of the verification chain.
requirements: stack is a pointer to a STACK_OF(X509) whose elements should be freed.
Frees both the stack structure and all X509 items it contains.
Behavior for stack == NULL is unknown (likely a no-op by convention); avoid passing invalid pointers.

functions.name: r_signature_error_quark
functions.description: Returns the GLib error domain quark used for RSignatureError errors. Use as the domain in GError APIs.

Use the returned GQuark as the error domain when checking/creating GError instances related to this API.

functions.description: Creates and configures an OpenSSL X509_STORE for certificate verification. If capath/cadir are NULL, default paths/options from configuration are used.
requirements: capath may be NULL to use defaults.

error may be NULL, or a location initialized to NULL (GLib convention).

requirements: content must be a valid GBytes containing the data to sign.
detached selects detached (TRUE) vs. embedded (FALSE) signature.

requirements: filename must point to an existing, readable file containing the data to sign.
certfile must be a path to a certificate file readable by the process.

functions.description: Appends a new signer to an existing CMS signature object using the provided certificate and private key, optionally including intermediates. Returns the updated signature.

functions.name: cms_is_detached

functions.name: cms_get_unverified_manifest
functions.description: Extracts a manifest embedded in a CMS signature without verifying it. Intended for inspection; do not rely on authenticity without verification.

manifest must be a non-NULL out-parameter to receive a GBytes* with the extracted manifest.
